## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Hud calls 'Ad to God  (`#hud-calls-ad`)

Cited ayat: 7:65, 7:69, 11:51-52, 26:123-130, 26:132-135, 46:21

> **7:65** وَإِلَىٰ عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥٓ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

> **7:69** أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَن جَآءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنكُمْ لِيُنذِرَكُمْ وَٱذْكُرُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَآءَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ بَصْۜطَةً فَٱذْكُرُوٓا۟ ءَالَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (7:65, 26:123-124): God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers.

**c2** (7:65): Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him.

**c3** (26:125-126): Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him.

**c4** (26:127, 11:51): Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds.

**c5** (11:52): Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength.

**c6** (11:52): Hud told them not to turn away as criminals.

**c7** (7:69): Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation.

**c8** (26:132-134): Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs.

**c9** (26:128-130): Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants.

**c10** (26:135): Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day.

**c11** (46:21): Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God.

### One-minute summary

God sent Hud to 'Ad, who called them to worship God alone and to fear Him [c1][c2][c3]. He asked no wage, reminded them of what God had given them and warned them of the punishment of a great day [c4][c8][c10].

### Complete story

God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers [c1]. Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him [c2]. Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him [c3]. Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds [c4]. Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength [c5]. Hud told them not to turn away as criminals [c6]. Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation [c7]. Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs [c8]. Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants [c9]. Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day [c10]. Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God [c11].

### Deep study

- God sent Hud to 'Ad; the ayat call Hud their brother, and 'Ad denied the messengers (7:65, 26:123-124) [c1].
- Hud told his people to worship God, for they had no deity other than Him, and asked whether they would not fear Him (7:65) [c2].
- Hud told them that he was a trustworthy messenger to them, and told them to fear God and to obey him (26:125-126) [c3].
- Hud told them that he asked them for no wage, because his wage was only with the Lord of the worlds (26:127, 11:51) [c4].
- Hud told them to ask forgiveness of their Lord and to turn back to Him, and said that He would then send abundant rain from the sky on them and add strength to their strength (11:52) [c5].
- Hud told them not to turn away as criminals (11:52) [c6].
- Hud told them to remember that God had made them successors after the people of Nuh and had increased them abundantly in creation (7:69) [c7].
- Hud told them to remember what God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs (26:132-134) [c8].
- Hud asked them whether they built a sign on every high ground for amusement, took up strong buildings in the hope of living on, and seized people as tyrants (26:128-130) [c9].
- Hud told them that he feared for them the punishment of a great day (26:135) [c10].
- Another passage speaks of the brother of 'Ad, who warned his people at al-Ahqaf, after warners had passed before him and after him, telling them to worship only God (46:21) [c11].

### Kids mode

God sent Hud to his people, the people of 'Ad [c1]. Hud told them to worship God alone [c2]. He reminded them of the good things God had given them: livestock, sons, gardens and springs [c8]. He also warned them of a great day of punishment [c10].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): Hud's reminder joins the gifts God had given with the call to worship Him [c8][c2]. One reading is that the passage asks the listener to look at what they have been given and to ask what it is for [c8][c9].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the Quran does not say where 'Ad lived beyond the single mention of al-Ahqaf, nor when, nor how many they were.
- Not established: whether the brother of 'Ad in 46:21 is the same person as Hud is not stated in that ayah; the draft reads it that way because 'Ad and Hud are joined in 7:65 and 26:124.
- Not established: what exactly the high ground (a word read in more than one way) and the strong buildings of 26:128-129 were.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the region where 'Ad lived, and any dates; none is used here.

## 2. How 'Ad answered  (`#the-answer-of-ad`)

Cited ayat: 7:66-68, 7:70-71, 11:53-57, 26:136-138, 41:15

> **7:66** قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِى سَفَاهَةٍ وَإِنَّا لَنَظُنُّكَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
>
> **7:67** قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِى سَفَاهَةٌ وَلَٰكِنِّى رَسُولٌ مِّن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
>
> **7:68** أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّى وَأَنَا۠ لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ

> **7:70** قَالُوٓا۟ أَجِئْتَنَا لِنَعْبُدَ ٱللَّهَ وَحْدَهُۥ وَنَذَرَ مَا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ
>
> **7:71** قَالَ قَدْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ رِجْسٌ وَغَضَبٌ أَتُجَٰدِلُونَنِى فِىٓ أَسْمَآءٍ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ فَٱنتَظِرُوٓا۟ إِنِّى مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُنتَظِرِينَ

> **11:53** قَالُوا۟ يَٰهُودُ مَا جِئْتَنَا بِبَيِّنَةٍ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **11:54** إِن نَّقُولُ إِلَّا ٱعْتَرَىٰكَ بَعْضُ ءَالِهَتِنَا بِسُوٓءٍ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشْهَدُوٓا۟ أَنِّى بَرِىٓءٌ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ
>
> **11:55** مِن دُونِهِۦ فَكِيدُونِى جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ لَا تُنظِرُونِ
>
> **11:56** إِنِّى تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ إِنَّ رَبِّى عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ

> **41:15** فَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ وَقَالُوا۟ مَنْ أَشَدُّ مِنَّا قُوَّةً أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَهُمْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَكَانُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (7:66): The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars.

**c2** (7:67-68): Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them.

**c3** (7:70): They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful.

**c4** (11:53): They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him.

**c5** (11:54): They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil.

**c6** (11:54-55): Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him.

**c7** (11:56): Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord.

**c8** (11:57): Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place.

**c9** (7:71): Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority.

**c10** (7:71): Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them.

**c11** (26:136-138): They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished.

**c12** (41:15): Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength.

**c13** (41:15): The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God.

### One-minute summary

The chiefs of 'Ad called Hud foolish and a liar, refused to leave their gods and told him to bring the punishment he threatened [c1][c3][c4]. Hud replied that he was a messenger, put his trust in God and told them to wait [c2][c7][c10].

### Complete story

The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars [c1]. Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them [c2]. They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful [c3]. They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him [c4]. They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil [c5]. Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him [c6]. Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord [c7]. Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place [c8]. Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority [c9]. Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them [c10]. They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished [c11]. Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength [c12]. The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God [c13].

### Deep study

- The chiefs of his people who disbelieved told Hud that they saw him in foolishness and thought him one of the liars (7:66) [c1].
- Hud answered that there was no foolishness in him but that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds who conveyed his Lord's messages and was a trustworthy adviser to them (7:67-68) [c2].
- They asked Hud whether he had come so that they should worship God alone and leave what their fathers worshipped, and told him to bring what he threatened if he was truthful (7:70) [c3].
- They told Hud that he had brought no clear proof, that they would not leave their gods on his word, and that they did not believe in him (11:53) [c4].
- They said that they could only say that some of their gods had struck Hud with evil (11:54) [c5].
- Hud called God to witness, and told them to bear witness, that he was free of what they set up with God besides Him (11:54-55) [c6].
- Hud told them that he had put his trust in God, his Lord and their Lord (11:56) [c7].
- Hud told them that if they turned away he had already conveyed what he was sent with, and that his Lord would make another people successors in their place (11:57) [c8].
- Hud told them that abomination and anger from their Lord had already fallen on them, and asked whether they disputed with him about names that they and their fathers had given, for which God had sent down no authority (7:71) [c9].
- Hud told them to wait, saying that he was waiting with them (7:71) [c10].
- They told Hud that it was the same to them whether he admonished them or was not one of those who admonish, that this was only the way of the earlier people, and that they would not be punished (26:136-138) [c11].
- Another passage says that 'Ad were arrogant in the land without right and said who was stronger than they in strength, and it asks whether they did not see that God who created them was stronger than they in strength (41:15) [c12].
- The same passage says that 'Ad used to reject the signs of God (41:15) [c13].

### Kids mode

Some of the people of 'Ad would not listen to Hud [c1]. They said they would not leave their gods [c4]. Hud said that he was a messenger and that he trusted God [c2][c7].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passages show a people who answered a call with insults and with loyalty to their fathers' ways [c1][c3]. One reading is that the same ayat show Hud answering without insult and returning to trust in God [c2][c7].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the speaker of the words 'rather it is what you sought to hasten' in 46:24 is not named; it is treated in the next chapter.
- Not established: the exact sense of the word translated abomination in 7:71 is read in more than one way, and the draft keeps the plain word.
- Not established: how long Hud spoke to them, how many believed, or who the chiefs were by name.
- Not established: the draft does not use 41:13-14, whose pronouns are not stated in those ayat; 41:15 names 'Ad.

### Claims

**c1** (11:58, 7:72): God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment.

**c2** (11:59): The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant.

**c3** (46:24): When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain.

**c4** (46:24): The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment.

**c5** (46:25): The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings.

**c6** (41:16, 54:19): God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world.

**c7** (51:41-42): The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed.

**c8** (69:7): God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees.

**c9** (69:8): The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen.

**c10** (46:26): God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them.

**c11** (11:60): A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud.

**c12** (53:50): The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad.

**c13** (89:6-8): Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land.

**c14** (26:139): The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers.

### One-minute summary

God saved Hud and those who believed with him by His mercy [c1]. A wind sent against 'Ad destroyed what it came upon, and the Quran calls their end a sign [c6][c7][c14].

### Complete story

God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment [c1]. The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant [c2]. When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain [c3]. The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment [c4]. The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings [c5]. God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world [c6]. The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed [c7]. God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees [c8]. The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen [c9]. God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them [c10]. A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud [c11]. The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad [c12]. Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land [c13]. The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers [c14].

### Deep study

- God saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Him, and saved them from a heavy punishment (11:58, 7:72) [c1].
- The Quran says that 'Ad rejected the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers and followed the order of every stubborn tyrant (11:59) [c2].
- When they saw it as a cloud coming toward their valleys, they said it was a cloud that would give them rain (46:24) [c3].
- The ayah answers that it was what they had asked to hasten: a wind carrying a painful punishment (46:24) [c4].
- The wind destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and they became people of whom nothing could be seen except their dwellings (46:25) [c5].
- God sent on them a furious wind in days of misfortune, to make them taste a punishment of disgrace in the life of this world (41:16, 54:19) [c6].
- The Quran calls the wind barren and says that it left nothing it came upon without making it like something decayed (51:41-42) [c7].
- God made the wind work against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and the ayah says that the people lay overthrown in it like hollow trunks of palm trees (69:7) [c8].
- The ayah then asks whether any remnant of them can be seen (69:8) [c9].
- God had given them hearing, sight and hearts, but these were of no use to them because they used to reject the signs of God, and what they used to mock at surrounded them (46:26) [c10].
- A curse followed them in this life and follows them on the Day of Resurrection, and the passage ends by saying away with 'Ad, the people of Hud (11:60) [c11].
- The Quran says that God destroyed the first 'Ad (53:50) [c12].
- Another passage asks whether the hearer has not seen how God dealt with 'Ad and names Iram, with pillars, the like of which was not created in the land (89:6-8) [c13].
- The Quran says that in their destruction there is a sign, and that most of them were not believers (26:139) [c14].

### Kids mode

God saved Hud and the people who believed with him [c1]. A strong wind came against 'Ad, and it did what God commanded [c5][c6]. The Quran calls what happened to them a sign [c14].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): The passage joins the rescue of the believers with the end of those who rejected the signs [c1][c10]. One reading is that hearing and sight are gifts, and that the ayah asks what a person does with them [c10].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where this happened, how long ago, or how many people were saved.
- Not established: whether Iram in 89:7 names a people, a place or both, how it relates to 'Ad, and what the pillars were; the ayat leave this open.
- Not established: the exact meaning of the first 'Ad in 53:50 and of the word for the wind (a furious or violent wind, read in more than one way).
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Iram with a particular city or region, and any date for the event.
